critical_code_review_comments: routers/reports.py line 101 logs `created_at` using `expires_at.isoformat()` — this is a copy-paste bug in the audit-log entry (both created_at and expires_at end up holding the expiry timestamp). Low-impact (audit-log only) but misleading; should be `datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()`.

routers/reports.py create_report_share_link reads `body = await request.json()` inside a try/except that swallows all exceptions. A legitimately malformed JSON body from the client will silently fall through to default ttl=168 rather than returning 400. Consider using a Pydantic body model with Optional[int] ttl_hours.

Cross-clinic 403 on /api/reports/{sid}/pdf was NOT directly asserted because the seed only provisions one clinic (clinic-acs-demo). The code-path guard at routers/reports.py:54-57 is correct-by-inspection, but a second clinic seed would enable a real test. Same applies to the share-link clinic-mismatch branch at lines 118-123.
share_token.py _secret() raises RuntimeError('JWT_SECRET not configured') but this surfaces as a 500 to the client. Consider catching and returning 503 with a clearer admin-facing message.

routers/reports.py _load_session_and_patient returns a fallback patient dict {patient_id: 'UNKNOWN', ...} when the patient is missing — this keeps PDFs renderable for orphaned sessions, but also bypasses the tenant check (since fallback has no clinic_id). An attacker aware of a session_id of a deleted-patient session could fetch its PDF. Consider requiring patient presence OR explicitly setting fallback.clinic_id = session.clinic_id.

share-link expiry returns 410 which is correct, but the audit collection report_share_links does not record revocation or access events. Consider adding a 'last_accessed_at' + 'access_count' $inc on successful fetch for HIPAA-style access logging.

billing.py still uses the legacy `_db()` helper (thin alias over get_db) while new routers use Depends(get_db) — mixed style. Next refactor should finish converging billing.py onto FastAPI DI for testability.
